definition: In this historical usage, acceptance was proposed as a better term than recognition for translating the German Anerkennung. It refers to a conceptual or philosophical sense of acknowledging or granting regard, rather than a clinical technique or diagnosis.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Acceptance; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not support the claim that the sense is “conceptual or philosophical” or that it specifically means “acknowledging or granting regard”; it only states that the term was recommended to replace “recognition” and is sometimes used to translate the German “Anerkennen(-ung).”
The packet does not provide any basis for contrasting acceptance with “a clinical technique or diagnosis,” which is not mentioned in the provided text.

The packet supports only that “Acceptance” was recommended as a replacement for “recognition” as a translation of German Anerkennen/Anerkennung, with a philosophical reference to Hegel and Eisler; it does not support the added gloss about “acknowledging or granting regard.”
The packet does not support the contrast with a “clinical technique or diagnosis,” so that part of the definition goes beyond the supplied source.
